name: Jasmine Crockett
role: U.S. Representative for Texas’s 30th district (2023–present); Texas state representative (2021–2023); lost the 2026 Democratic Senate primary
summary: Dallas-area Democrat and former public defender and civil-rights attorney who is a staunch Democratic partisan on voting rights, abortion, gun control, health care and immigration enforcement. She cosponsors Medicare for All, backs higher taxes on the wealthy and a higher minimum wage, and opposes cuts to SNAP and Medicaid. She opposes ICE funding and the Trump administration’s tariffs and war powers, and favors Supreme Court expansion and filibuster carve-outs for voting rights.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Told the Texas Tribune she cosponsors Medicare for All and supports a single-payer system with no premiums, deductibles or co-pays.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Her House website calls her a staunch advocate for raising the minimum wage; Wikipedia notes she backs raising it above $7.25.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Wants the corporate rate for the largest firms restored, billionaires to pay more, and a return to Clinton-era rates; voted against H.R. 1 citing tax breaks for billionaires.

unions-good.rationale: Her website says she is a believer in the power of unions so that workers are on equal footing with those in power.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Says AI needs federal regulation to protect consumers and workers and offered an amendment strengthening crypto regulation; backs vigorous antitrust enforcement.

cut-welfare.rationale: Voted against H.R. 1 and the 2023 budget deal, calling SNAP and Medicaid cuts and work requirements cruel; describes the programs as lifelines.

strong-leader.rationale: Repeatedly criticizes presidents acting around Congress (war powers, tariffs) and says Congress must be a check on the president.

limit-guns.rationale: Supports an assault weapons ban and universal background checks; also says she owns guns and is licensed to carry, and that Democrats do not want to take everyone’s guns.

empower-police-military.rationale: No stated position on police and military funding or authority as a whole; calls for police accountability are something nearby.

rehabilitation.rationale: Says she is working on legislation to update outdated systems and reduce recidivism; as a Texas legislator co-authored reentry measures cutting fees for recently incarcerated people.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Website says she is fighting to protect same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Calls herself an outspoken believer in the right to choose; says only the woman should have the final say and works to protect abortion at the federal level.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Introduced a resolution for a commission examining systemic racism and persisting racial inequities; led letter seeking clemency over crack sentencing disparities.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Favors a path to citizenship, extending TPS and a faster, more accessible legal system, and opposes mass enforcement; has not said levels should rise, so only -1.

open-borders.rationale: Says border security and comprehensive reform go hand in hand and backs technology to remove "bad actors" while processing asylum faster; does not call for open borders.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Website calls climate change an existential crisis and says she will lead the charge on electrification and a just transition; also backs "all of the above" energy.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Condemned 2025 tariffs as costs borne by importers, businesses and consumers and introduced a bill refunding tariffs; did not address protection of industry as such.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Said she could not vote for the "punitive, ineffective, and needlessly cruel" SNAP work requirements in the 2023 budget agreement.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Backs an "all of the above" energy approach and Texas oil and gas, but opposes drilling on public lands and favors renewables.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Cosponsored impeachment of the DHS secretary over ICE abuses and demands accountability for police use of force; statements concern current rather than past abuses.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Statements invoke "Equal Justice Under Law" and say no one is above the law, including immigrants entitled to due process.

separated-powers.rationale: Repeatedly says Congress must check the president and that courts and Congress hold executive power to account.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Said with colleagues that "there is strength in diversity" and that inclusion strengthens national security.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Says everyone, including immigrants, is entitled to due process under the Constitution and that the U.S. does not suspend civil rights for political points.

party-controls-media.rationale: Introduced the Free Speech Act to stop the FCC being used to push a president’s political views on media companies, calling such overreach a step toward authoritarianism.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: No stated position on residence requirements; criticism of naturalisation backlogs and costs is something nearby.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Wants rates raised on the wealthiest and a return to Clinton-era rates, the opposite of a flat tax.

ban-cartels.rationale: Says monopolies hinder competition and should be broken up, with antitrust laws enforced vigorously.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Interview comments treat the prospect of the Supreme Court ending affirmative action as a setback and "ridiculous"; has not addressed hiring specifically.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Website says she fights employment discrimination and demands that discrimination and bigotry be treated as crimes.

corporate-influence.rationale: Says she supports efforts to root out corruption and the influence of big money and shady private interests in politics.

job-guarantee.rationale: No stated position on a job guarantee; calling a good job a human right is a general principle.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: No statement addresses criminalisation; support for LGBTQ protections is a general principle here.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Condemned the expulsion of two Black Tennessee legislators as silencing voices pushing back.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Opposes Republican anti-trans legislation and says Democrats were distracted by trans-athlete bans; no statement specifically on legal recognition.

racial-franchise.rationale: Calls Voting Rights Act Section 2 essential against the denial of Black Americans’ voice and supports restoring and strengthening it.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Website says she believes in eliminating student loan debt; also cites student loan forgiveness as popular.

voter-id.rationale: Called the SAVE America Act a voter-suppression bill; backed federal bills to expand access (vote by mail, online registration, short lines).

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Says systemic racism has impacted Black Americans and that racial inequities persist today.

notes: Announced a U.S. Senate run in December 2025 and lost the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary to James Talarico; she remains in the House through 2026. Her Israel position is mixed (support for Israeli civilians and allies, votes for aid, but a 2024 letter urging limits on weapons transfers and statements that aid should stop if international law is violated), so no Israel statement is answered. Medical-cannabis expansion (Texas HB 1535, 2021) is not a position on recreational legalization.
